reference.title: Barbell JM-Bench Press
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the bar comes down toward the upper chest and chin, breathe out as you press.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.2 s up

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9). Start well below your close-grip bench press: elbow-dominant pressing is hard on the elbows (clinical opinion).
prescription.progression: More reps, then 1.25-2.5 kg; keep the bar path the same.

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench, feet planted. Grip the bar overhand a little inside shoulder width, unrack it and hold it over the shoulders, elbows tucked and pointing toward the feet.
Breathe in and let the elbows bend and travel down toward the feet together, so the bar comes back toward the upper chest and chin (half press, half skull crusher).
Bar a few centimetres above the upper chest / chin, forearms angled back, elbows pointing toward the feet; no contact with the face.
Breathe out and push the bar back up, straightening the elbows as the upper arms return to vertical.
Arms straight over the shoulders; re-brace and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Turning it into a close-grip press (elbows flaring, bar to the lower chest)
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows tucked and let the bar come back toward the chin.

mistakes.mistake: Turning it into a skull crusher (upper arms still)
mistakes.fix: Let the elbows travel down toward the feet as the forearms fold back; both joints move.

mistakes.mistake: Bar dropping onto the face or throat
mistakes.fix: Lower under control to just above the upper chest; use a lighter bar.
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms.
Progress slowly; elbow-dominant pressing loads the elbow joint (clinical opinion).

kinematics.norm: A little inside shoulder width; narrow grips raised triceps activity (Saeterbakken 2021)
From straight to deeply bent (about 110-130 degrees) at the bottom (clinical opinion; no measured norm found)
The upper arms tilt toward the feet as the elbows bend, about 40-55 degrees from vertical at the bottom (clinical opinion); the poster in Puluka reports less shoulder involvement than a regular press
Bar travels back toward the upper chest and chin, not the face (clinical opinion)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees, like the bench set-up in Solstad 2020
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell JM-Bench Press, video (movement reference)
Puluka, JM press vs skull crusher movement analysis (student biomechanics poster, Monmouth University; one male participant, surface EMG normalised to MVIC)

Saeterbakken, Stien, Pedersen, Solstad, Cumming and Andersen 2021, the effect of grip width on muscle strength and electromyographic activity in bench press among novice- and resistance-trained men (Int J Environ Res Public Health 18(12):6444; PMC8296276)

Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, ACE-sponsored; 15 women, 8 exercises at 70% 1RM)

Solstad, Andersen, Shaw, Hoel, Vonheim and Saeterbakken 2020, a comparison of muscle activation between barbell bench press and dumbbell flyes in resistance-trained males (J Sports Sci Med 19(4):645-651; PMC7675616)

cautions: Press with a spotter, or in a rack with the safety arms set just below the chest; never use collars without a spotter or safeties (clinical opinion).
Set the hooks so you can unrack the bar with nearly straight arms; move the bar over the shoulders before lowering and back over the hooks before re-racking.
The bar travels toward the face: use a spotter and a load you fully control (clinical opinion).
Elbow pain: stop, lighten the load or switch to a close-grip press (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Elbow discomfort: shorter range (stop higher above the chest) or an EZ bar.
regressions: Barbell skull crusher with a light bar.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Main mover: a hybrid of a close-grip press and a lying extension, mostly elbow extension. In a one-person biomechanics poster the JM press gave higher triceps EMG than the skull crusher (Puluka); narrow-grip pressing also raises triceps activity (Saeterbakken 2021).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Main mover: a hybrid of a close-grip press and a lying extension, mostly elbow extension. In a one-person biomechanics poster the JM press gave higher triceps EMG than the skull crusher (Puluka); narrow-grip pressing also raises triceps activity (Saeterbakken 2021).
muscleNotes.pec_r: Helps press the upper arms back up from the tucked position.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Helps press the upper arms back up from the tucked position.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder as the elbows come down and back up.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder as the elbows come down and back up.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades set on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades set on the bench.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Control the elbows as they travel toward the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Control the elbows as they travel toward the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the pelvis on the bench.

phases.label: Arms straight, bar over the shoulders

guides.label: Elbows deeply bent at the bottom
